headline: Your left wrist is still healing after your broken bone and surgery, and your doctor is working to get you approved for hand therapy so you can regain your strength and movement.

sections.whats_going_on: Back in November 2025, you broke a bone near your left wrist (the distal radius). You had surgery shortly after to fix the break with hardware (metal plates or screws), and that hardware was later removed. At today's visit, your doctor found that your left wrist still has limited movement — you cannot fully bend, straighten, or move it side to side — and you are still feeling pain that you rated as 5 to 6 out of 10. This is expected given your injury and surgery. The rest of your arm, shoulder, neck, and right hand all checked out fine.
sections.your_plan: Your doctor is requesting approval from your workers' compensation insurance for occupational (hand) therapy — 2 sessions per week for 3 weeks — to help you regain movement, grip strength, and dexterity in your left wrist and hand. A hand therapy prescription was given to you today. Your left wrist brace is now optional; you can wear it or not, depending on what feels best for you. You may also wrap your left wrist with an elastic bandage for light support and comfort if you choose. At work, you are still on modified duty and are limited to one hour of work. Your doctor also sent a formal letter to your workers' compensation insurance carrier addressing the delay in your care and requesting they move forward with authorization.
sections.medications: No new medicines were prescribed at today's visit. Keep taking any medicines you are already using, the same way as before.
sections.follow_up: You will see Dr. Sabbag again in six weeks for a repeat evaluation of your left wrist.
sections.when_to_seek_help: The note did not list specific warning signs to watch for. If your pain gets worse, you notice new symptoms, or you have any concerns before your next appointment, call the clinic.
